lead: `git commit -F .agent-tmp/<name>.txt` can silently commit a *previous* session's message.
body: `.agent-tmp/` is not cleaned between sessions and every session reaches for the same obvious file names, so a `-F` naming a file you did not write this session succeeds with someone else's subject line, and `git commit -F msg.txt 2>/dev/null || true` hides even the missing-file case. Write the message file in the same call sequence you commit it in, under a name new to this session, and never mask a `git commit`'s exit status; `session.py --wrap` is immune.
